newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: ECNZ to invest $50 mln in upgrading power scheme.
newsitem.headline: ECNZ to invest $50 mln in upgrading power scheme.

text.p: Electricity Corporation of New Zealand (ECNZ) said on Wednesday it is to invest $50 million in upgrading the Waitaki hydro power scheme.

Kieran Devine, general manager of generation, said an increase of at least 1 percent efficiency from the power scheme is expected to result from this project, which would equate to an increase in output of 125 gigawatt hours. This is enough to meet the domestic consumption of 16,000 households.
The project will introduce automation and remote control systems for the eight Waitaki hydro-electric power stations, allowing them to be controlled from Twizel.
A $20 million contract has been signed with United States companies Voith Hydro and Landis and Gyr, which will be responsible for upgrading the existing hydro schemes automation systems.

Devine said the control systems for the upper Waitaki stations were now nearing the end of their economic life, while the mid-Waitaki stations of Benmore, Aviemore and Waitaki were to be automated enabling them to be remote controlled from Twizel.
The eight stations involved produce about 30 percent of New Zealand's annual electricity consumption.

The project also includes the installation of a new 180 km fibre optic network to link the eight stations, the renewal of some electrical plant to ensure future low maintenance costs and additional control centre software.
The project is scheduled for completion in June 1999.
